worked.problem: Rectangle ABCD has AB=6 cm and BC=5 cm. Find AC and state why BD has the same length.
actions: Draw the four right angles of rectangle ABCD.
Label AB=6 cm and BC=5 cm.
In right triangle ABC, AC²=6²+5²=61.
AC=√61 cm; the diagonals of a rectangle are equal.
Answer: AC = BD = √61 cm. Square the diagonal to check the two side squares.
worked.check: Answer: AC = BD = √61 cm. Square the diagonal to check the two side squares.
worked.misconception: Use only marked geometric facts, state the theorem, and keep corresponding vertices in order.

worked.problem: Rhombus ABCD has diagonals AC=8 cm and BD=8 cm. Find its area and name the diagonal angle.
actions: Draw a rhombus and mark all four sides equal.
Label diagonals AC=8 cm and BD=8 cm.
Rhombus diagonals bisect at right angles, forming four right triangles.
Area=½×8×8=32 cm².
Answer: area = 32 cm²; diagonals perpendicular. Their lengths need not be equal.
worked.check: Answer: area = 32 cm²; diagonals perpendicular. Their lengths need not be equal.
worked.misconception: Use only marked geometric facts, state the theorem, and keep corresponding vertices in order.

worked.problem: Square ABCD has side AB=8 cm. Find its area and state one diagonal property.
actions: Draw a square with four equal sides and four right angles.
Label each side 8 cm.
Area=side×side=8×8.
The diagonals are equal and meet at right angles.
Answer: area = 64 cm²; diagonals equal and perpendicular. This square has both rectangle and rhombus diagonal properties.
